sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [page dated 2024-06-25]. 'Nakai', 'Nakai-Naki', 'Naki'. Newguineaworld (Santa Fe Institute; UZH mirror).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States 'There is no published phonology of Nakai. Based upon comparason to Naki and Tangko, Nakai likely has 10 or 12 consonants and 5 vowels' and 'No phonology of Naki is provided in Wilbrink (2004) or Williamson (2010.)'. Lists as the only sources Jang 2003: 39-47, Wilbrink 2004: 109a-110f, Hughes 2009: 27-37, Williamson 2010 (unpublished Nagi grammar).

sources.citation: Lebold, Randy, Ron Kriens, Myo-Sook Sohn & Yunita Susanto. 2014. Report on the Upper Digul Helicopter Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2014-002. Dallas: SIL International. 35 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Sec. 5.3 (pp. 9-11) treats Nakai (Burunggop, Awimbon) and Nagi (Tarngop, Kawor, Itutamon) as probably one language (63% lexical similarity); fn. 14: 'pronounced [naɣai] or [naʁai]'. Appendix B (p. 25) lexical-similarity rules: 'Unreleased consonants, accents and nasalized vowels are ignored.' Appendix C (pp. 26-34): Nagi/Tarngop (239 items) and Nakai/Awimbon (50 items) wordlists in IPA with primary-stress marks (ˈmitɔ 'nose', ˈkerkor 'mouth', semˈber 'fingernail'), mostly penultimate by rough tally; no analysis.

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 2009. Upper Digul Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-003. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 'NAKAI' section (printed pp. 13-14) is sociolinguistic only ('The language has never been.'); Appendix V (pp. 27-37) gives a 239-item Nakai/Burunggop wordlist in IPA with primary-stress marks (ʔɑˈβɔt 'head', ˈmitɔ 'nose', ˈniŋgi 'tooth', sɛmˈbɛt 'fingernail') but no analysis; the words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the report. Rough script tally of the marked polysyllables: 122 penult, 36 final, 8 antepenult, 3 earlier (observation on the data, not a source statement).
